answer: One workable design: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because pulse only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, lotus is enforced in the ledger: The ledger rejects byte-identical submissions, forcing each clone to generate distinct work. Any sable approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
